lead_headline: Restaurant tracker stays silent for second straight day — zero new leads as July 4 weekend extends the freeze across all consumer-facing intelligence.

restaurant.blurb: 0 new leads today. Active leads: 271 (147 openings, 124 closures). The holiday weekend extends the drought — two consecutive zero-lead days, longest since April.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications — the freeze now hits 37 days. No bar, restaurant, or retail license filings since early June. The July 4 holiday adds another day to what's now the longest application drought on record. The 12,325-license database historically processes 2-4 weekly applications even during summer lulls, making this six-week silence unprecedented. Whether driven by extended holiday closures, capital constraints, or state administrative backlogs, the pipeline remains frozen. The next filing will reset the clock on a licensing slowdown without modern precedent.

reputation.blurb: 1 mention yesterday — a single Facebook pickup as the July 4 holiday weekend suppresses media activity. The week closes at 73 mentions across 17 sources, up 26% from last week's 58. Facebook dominates with 26 citations, Reddit contributes 17, Instagram and X.com add 6 each, Hoodline runs 3. Google News RSS delivered 71 of 73 discoveries. Broncos headquarters investment, Inspirato sponsorship exit, and German grocer Aldi's Colorado entry drove the week's strongest engagement. The holiday weekend typically suppresses citation velocity — Monday's resumption will clarify whether the uptrend holds or the late-June surge was transient.

subscriptions.blurb: Net −1 yesterday (0 new, 1 canceled) nudges MTD down to +9 (+2.2/day). 90-day net: +117. The third straight day of zero or negative net (Wed −1, Thu −1, Fri −1) breaks the late-June momentum that peaked June 30 with +13. The 7-day window still shows strength (+27 net vs. prior week's −5), but three consecutive flat/negative days suggest the explosive June 29-30 surge (+17 in two days) was an anomaly, not a trend shift. July's pace (+2.2/day) still outpaces YTD baseline (+1.3/day), but the recent stall mirrors the pattern that preceded June's −9 week. Holiday weekend timing complicates the read — Monday's numbers will clarify whether this is seasonal noise or a genuine momentum reversal.
